title: HACCP — Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
shortDescription: The seven principles, twelve application steps, CCP decision logic and worked examples.
genZNote: HACCP: what can go wrong, where do you stop it, prove you stopped it. Seven principles, one logic chain — learn the order.

sections.heading: Origin and Idea
sections.body: HACCP was developed in the 1960s by Pillsbury with NASA and the US Army Natick Labs to ensure safe space food; it is a preventive, science-based system recommended by Codex and required by many national regulations. In India, FSSAI Schedule 4 and licensing conditions expect HACCP-based food safety systems for specified categories; ISO 22000 incorporates HACCP principles (see the ISO lessons for the standard itself).

steps.name: 1 Conduct hazard analysis
steps.explanation: Identify hazards and control measures at each step.

steps.name: 2 Determine CCPs
steps.purpose: Find control points essential to safety.

steps.name: 3 Establish critical limits
steps.explanation: Measurable limits e.g. 72 °C for 15 s, pH ≤ 4.6.

steps.name: 4 Monitoring
steps.explanation: Continuous or frequent measurement and recording.

sections.heading: Twelve Codex Steps and Examples
bullets: Preliminary tasks: assemble team, describe product, identify intended use, construct and confirm flow diagram, then apply the seven principles.
Example CCP — milk pasteurization: hazard pathogens; critical limit 72 °C for 15 s; monitor temperature chart; deviation → divert flow/repasteurise; verification by alkaline phosphatase test.
Example CCP — canning: retort time/temperature; metal detection for foreign matter.
CCP vs OPRP: a CCP has a critical limit and is essential for control; OPRPs are control measures with action criteria managed within PRPs (ISO 22000 terminology).
HACCP limits: does not replace GMP/PRPs, requires trained team and management commitment.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: HACCP is a systematic preventive approach that identifies, evaluates and controls significant food-safety hazards at critical control points.

commonTraps: Do not say HACCP replaces PRPs.
Do not claim HACCP is an ISO standard.
mustRemember: Principle order: analysis, CCP, limits, monitoring, corrective action, verification, records.

sources.name: Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene (CXC 1-1969)
